title: 2009 AMC 10B Problem 4
statement: A rectangular yard contains two flower beds in the shape of congruent isosceles right triangles. The remainder of the yard has a trapezoidal shape, as shown. The parallel sides of the trapezoid have lengths \(15\) and \(25\) meters. What fraction of the yard is occupied by the flower beds?

solutions.text:
The two parallel sides differ by \(25-15=10,\) split evenly between the two triangles, so each isosceles right triangle has legs of length \(5\) and area \(\dfrac12\cdot5^2=\dfrac{25}{2}.\)

Together the beds cover \(25\) square meters. The rectangle has length \(25\) and width \(5,\) so area \(125.\) The fraction is \(\dfrac{25}{125}=\dfrac15.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Each triangle’s legs are half of \(25-15\)
Compare the total triangle area to the full rectangle of dimensions \(25\times5\)
